chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who died and left heirs, and one of the heirs acknowledged a debt on behalf of his father: 'That debt binds him only within his share, to the extent of what he inherited, and does not bind him in all his property.' If two of the heirs acknowledged it and were just (adl), it was accepted as binding on all the heirs; but if they were not just, they were bound only in their shares to the extent of what they inherited. Similarly, if some of the heirs acknowledged the existence of a brother or sister, it binds them only within their share.

And Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever acknowledges a brother for himself, he is a partner in the property but his lineage is not established. If two acknowledge him, it is the same, unless they are just, in which case his lineage is established and he is included in the inheritance with them.'
ai.seo_question: How is a deceased father's debt handled among heirs if only one heir acknowledges it?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details Imam Ali’s (AS) juridical reasoning on debt and lineage, distinguishing between individual liability and collective estate binding based on the number and justice ('adl) of acknowledging heirs. It highlights the Shia principle that a single heir’s confession is limited to his share, whereas two just heirs can establish lineage or bind the entire estate, reflecting the interplay between personal testimony and communal inheritance rights.
